# OS

This folder holds personal machine setup, bootstrap scripts, and reusable workstation tooling for this repo owner.

It is intentionally different from the Smash Ultimate code and content in the rest of the repository:

- Use `.os/` for Linux or Omarchy setup, machine-specific helper scripts, and reproducible local environment setup.
- Do not treat `.os/` as part of the Smash Ultimate website, Python analysis packages, or Reflex app code unless the user explicitly asks for an integration.
- Favor clear setup documentation so a new laptop or desktop can be configured the same way.

## New machine

On a fresh Omarchy install (it ships `git` but not `uv`):

```bash
git clone <repo> ~/repos/delulu-smash && ~/repos/delulu-smash/.os/install.sh
```

`install.sh` gives the machine both the delulu-smash framework and the OS setup. It installs `uv`, runs the
root `.install.sh` (Python environment with `uv sync`, the pre-commit git hook, git-lfs and the LFS data
files, then `ds settings sync`, which asks for the Pydantic AI Gateway key; `Ctrl+D` skips it and
`ds settings sync` stores it later), then runs `os sync`. If the framework step fails it stops there; fix
the cause and run it again. On a machine that has never synced, `os sync`:

1. lists everything that differs from the list (theme, default apps, keybindings) and offers one answer for
   the lot: `d` = use the list's (the replaced files are backed up),
2. shows the full plan (packages, plugins, web apps, files, settings, the `source .os/rc` line for
   `~/.bashrc`) and asks "Apply?".

After that, open a new terminal and use `os sync`.

Manual per-machine steps (not synced):

- Sign in to 1Password. (The master password for `os pwd-copy` lives in the per-machine keyring; `os sync`
  offers `os pwd-store` while none is stored, or run it yourself.) Also turn on Settings > Developer >
  Integrate with 1Password CLI, so `ds settings sync` can read the API keys from 1Password.
- Monitors / scaling (`~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua`) and input tweaks (`input.lua`).

## Everyday use: `os sync`

One command, on whichever machine you are at. `.os/machine.toml` is the one list of what every machine should
have; `os sync` makes the machine and the list the same **in both directions** (`--dry-run` previews: it asks
nothing and changes nothing).

1. `git pull --rebase` (skip with `--no-pull`). If the repo has uncommitted edits, it lists them and asks
   whether to commit them all (you type the message) and then pull; no (or `--yes`) skips the pull and
   syncs with the list as it is here (`--dry-run` also skips it).
2. **Changes made on this machine** since its last sync (installed or removed a package, created a web app,
   edited `bindings.lua`, switched theme, ...): asks about each one.
   - `k` keep: save it to the list, so the other machine gets it.
   - `d` discard: undo it here (uninstall, restore the list's version; files are backed up first).
   - `i` ignore (packages and web apps): add to `[ignore]`, never synced or asked about again.
   - `s` skip (the default): leave it, ask again next time.
   - More than 3 new packages or web apps: one answer for all of them is offered too (each, keep all,
     discard all = remove them all here after a confirm listing them, ignore all, skip all).
3. **Changes that came from the list** (what the other machine saved, or a hand edit of `machine.toml`): shows
   the plan and asks "Apply?". This includes removals: a package you removed and saved on one machine is
   removed on the other.
4. Shows the `.os/` files it will commit (**only `.os/`**; other changes stay out) and any other unpushed
   commits a push would also send, then asks "Commit and push?".

Good to know:

- The same thing changed on both machines: it shows both versions and asks which one wins.
- Something fails to apply (eg an AUR package that no longer builds): the rest still applies, the command
  exits with an error, and the next `os sync` asks what to do with the leftover (`k` removes it from the list).
- `--yes` asks nothing: it applies the list's changes and skips this machine's own changes. It never pushes
  commits other than its own.
- How it tells "changed here" from "changed on the other machine": each machine records the commit it last
  synced to in `~/.local/state/delulu-os/synced`. Files it replaces are backed up under
  `~/.local/state/delulu-os/backup/<time>/`.
- Applying goes through Omarchy's own commands (`omarchy pkg add`, `omarchy webapp install`,
  `omarchy theme set`, ...), so it keeps working with Omarchy updates. If an update renames one of those
  commands, `os sync` says which and changes nothing.

### Saving changes without the questions: `os save`

`os save` saves this machine's changes to the list: the same as answering `k` in `os sync`, but without a
question per change. With no names it saves every change made here since the last sync; with names, only
those. If it saved anything, it then shows what a commit would contain (everything changed in `.os/`, staged or not; other staged
files are listed but left out) plus any unpushed commits, and asks "Commit and push?". It never pulls or
applies anything from the list (that's `os sync`). AI agents use `--no-commit` to name what they changed,
right after a change you asked for.

```bash
os save --dry-run                        # what a full save would do
os save                                  # every change made here, then "Commit and push?"
os save --no-commit package:zed          # only write .os/ (no commit, no question)
os save package:zed                      # just installed (or removed) a package
os save file:.config/hypr/bindings.lua   # edited a tracked file; a new path starts being tracked
os save webapp:Twitch setting:theme toggle:window-no-gaps
```

- Kinds: `package`, `plugin`, `webapp`, `file`, `setting`, `toggle`, `bar`. `--dry-run` previews.
- `--no-commit`: the next `os sync` or `os save` commits it. A rejected push (remote ahead) means run
  `os sync`, which pulls first.
- "Every change" includes removals: a listed package you uninstalled here is taken off the list for all
  machines. Preview with `--dry-run` first.
- Anything the list changed since this machine last synced (or everything, if it never synced) is left for
  `os sync` to ask about, since saving would undo the other machine's change. With names it refuses
  outright; without, it saves the rest and lists those.

### The list: `.os/machine.toml`

| Section      | What                                                | Example                                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `[packages]` | `pacman` and `aur` packages beyond stock Omarchy    | `"glow"`                                        |
| `[packages.desktop]` / `[packages.laptop]` | packages for one role only | `"obs-studio"` (desktop)               |
| `[ignore]`   | packages / web apps never synced                    | hardware packages, Omarchy's default web apps   |
| `[settings]` | theme, font, default browser / editor / terminal    | `theme = "Everforest"`                          |
| `[bar]`      | bar widget options                                  | `"omarchy.clock.format" = "dddd M/d HH:mm"`     |
| `[toggles]`  | Omarchy Hyprland toggles: `"on"` / `"off"`          | `"window-no-gaps" = "on"`                       |
| `[plugins]`  | Omarchy plugins: id = git URL                       | `"hamsti.vitals" = "https://..."`               |
| `[files]`    | files synced between `$HOME` and `.os/files/`       | `".config/hypr/bindings.lua" = "always"`        |
| `[webapps]`  | web apps: name = URL                                | `"Twitch" = "https://www.twitch.tv/"`           |

- Editing the list by hand is fine: the next `os sync` applies the edit.
- **Track another file:** add `"<path under $HOME>" = "always"` under `[files]`, then `os sync` (answer `k`).
  Only files you own belong here (overrides like `bindings.lua`), written with `$HOME` /
  `os.getenv("HOME")` instead of `/home/<user>` so they work on every machine.
- **A file for one machine only:** use `"lspci:<text>"` instead of `"always"`; it then applies only where
  `lspci` output contains `<text>` (hostname is no use: every fresh Omarchy install is named `omarchy`).
- **Desktop or laptop only:** each machine has a role in the git-ignored `.os/local.toml`
  (`role = "desktop"`), asked on its first `os sync` / `os save` (the guess: a battery means a laptop).
  `os role` shows it, `os role laptop` changes it. Packages under `[packages.<role>]` are installed only on
  that role's machines; a file entry can say `"desktop"` / `"laptop"` instead of `"always"`. When sync asks
  about a new package, `[o]nly desktops` saves it to this role's section instead of the shared list.
- `[toggles]` names are the files in `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/toggles/` (not `flags.lua`, a
  placeholder). `window-no-gaps` is the look without gaps, borders or rounded corners between windows
  (`SUPER + SHIFT + BACKSPACE` flips it).
- Web app icons are not synced: each machine fetches the site's own icon when it installs the web app, so
  an icon can differ between machines. If a site's icon can't be fetched, that web app isn't installed and
  `os sync` reports it.
- Not in the list on purpose: monitors, input tweaks, secrets.

## Files

- `.os/install.sh`: first-run bootstrap (installs uv, runs the root `.install.sh`, then `sync`).
- `.os/cli.py`: `os` CLI: `sync`, `save`, `pwd-store`, `pwd-copy`.
- `.os/machine.toml`: the list (see above).
- `.os/files/`: the tracked files, at their path under `$HOME`. Currently:
  - `.config/hypr/bindings.lua`: custom keybindings. Each binding that replaces a default has a
    `-- previously: X` comment.
  - `.config/chromium-flags.conf`: only on machines with the AMD Raphael iGPU (VP9 flicker workaround).
  - `.claude/settings.json`: Claude Code's user settings (every project, in Zed and in a terminal); its
    hooks call `agent-notify.sh` below.
- `.os/rc`: bashrc additions (`os` / `ds` aliases, start in this repo).
- `.os/scripts/keybindings/`: scripts called by keybindings:
  - `screenrecord.sh`: region recording toggle (`SUPER + SHIFT + Q`, `--save` on `SUPER + SHIFT + ALT + Q`).
  - `claude-delulu.sh`: Claude Code in this repo, continuing the last session (`SUPER + SHIFT + A`).
  - `pwd-copy.sh`: copies the 1Password master password via `os pwd-copy` (`SUPER + SHIFT + P`).
- `.os/scripts/hooks/`: scripts called by AI agent hooks:
  - `agent-notify.sh`: an Omarchy notification when Claude needs you (a permission prompt, a question, a
    plan to approve, a finished turn). Zed can't send desktop notifications itself (only its own pop-up,
    `agent.notify_when_agent_waiting`), so this comes from Claude Code's hooks, which Zed's Claude agent
    loads too. A finished turn is skipped while Zed is focused; a click focuses Zed. Other Zed agents
    (not Claude) are not covered.
- `.os/scripts/`: other machine helper scripts not bound to keys.

## Known machine issues

- **Desktop (AMD Raphael iGPU + NVIDIA RTX 5060): video flicker in Chromium.** AMD VCN hardware VP9 decode
  corrupts video (YouTube/Twitch). Workaround: `--disable-accelerated-video-decode` in
  `~/.config/chromium-flags.conf` (tracked, applied only on this GPU via `lspci:Raphael` in `machine.toml`). Also don't set
  `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` etc. globally in `envs.conf`: it routes decode to the idle NVIDIA GPU and crashes
  Chromium.
  - To try later (deliberately; it needs a reboot): first check Mesa release notes for a VCN/VP9 fix. If none,
    boot with the `amd_iommu=off` kernel param (gives up IOMMU device isolation), remove the flag, retest
    playback and `chrome://gpu`. Revert the param if it doesn't help.
- **Nintendo Switch (OmniRCM): "✗ No Tegra RCM device found" while the log says "RCM device connected".**
  A permission problem, not the cable: see [FAQ: Nintendo Switch (OmniRCM)](#faq-nintendo-switch-omnircm).

## FAQ: Nintendo Switch (OmniRCM)

OmniRCM sends a payload (eg hekate) to a Switch in RCM (recovery) mode over USB. The binary lives in
git-ignored `local/omnircm/OmniRCM-linux-x64`, opened from the launcher as "OmniRCM (Switch)" (this laptop
only: `os sync` tracks neither).

**First time on a machine?** Open OmniRCM, click the red `Setup udev` button, enter the password, then
restart the computer once (`id` should then list `nintendo_switch`).

**Every time after that:**

1. Open "OmniRCM (Switch)" from the launcher, with the Switch unplugged.
2. Put the Switch in RCM: hold Power ~12 s until it is fully off, jig in the right Joy-Con rail, hold
   **Vol+** and press **Power**. The screen stays black (a Nintendo logo means it booted normally: redo it).
3. Plug it into the laptop directly (not through a hub or the Ethernet adapter).
4. The log shows "RCM device connected", then auto-injects (or click `Inject Payload`): hekate boots.

**The log says "RCM device connected" but then "✗ No Tegra RCM device found".** The app can *see* the
Switch (listing USB devices needs no permission) but can't *open* it to send the payload. Linux USB devices
belong to root unless a udev rule says otherwise; `Setup udev` writes `/etc/udev/rules.d/70-switch.rules`
(the Switch's `APX` device → group `nintendo_switch`) and adds you to that group. Until you have logged in
again, the app doesn't have that group yet, and the open fails. A Mac needs none of this: macOS lets any app
open a USB device.

**Why does it need a restart (or a log out and back in)?** A process's groups are a list fixed when it
starts, copied from its parent, and only the login reads `/etc/group` to build the first list. Everything
after that (Hyprland, kitty, the shell, OmniRCM) inherits a copy. `Setup udev` changed `/etc/group`, but no
running process re-reads it, so nothing started in that login can get the new group. A new login builds the
list again, with `nintendo_switch` in it. Check with `id` (your shell's groups) against
`getent group nintendo_switch` (what's on disk):

```bash
id                              # this session: no nintendo_switch yet → restart
getent group nintendo_switch    # on disk: nintendo_switch:x:1003:<you>
grep Groups /proc/$(pgrep -f OmniRCM-linux)/status   # the running app's groups (need 1003)
```

**Do I have to restart every time?** No, once. The membership is saved in `/etc/group`, so every later
login has it. What does repeat: entering RCM on the Switch (off, jig in, hold Vol+, press Power: the screen
stays black), each time.

**Can I skip the restart?** Usually `newgrp nintendo_switch` (or `sg`) starts a shell with the new group,
but Arch has no `sg`, and `newgrp` did not add the group here (2026-11-20). Restart.

**Should I click `Setup udev` again?** No: once per machine is enough, and running it again changes
nothing. `os sync` can't track it (it writes outside `$HOME`), so do it once on each new machine.

**Still "✗ No Tegra RCM device found" after the restart, with `nintendo_switch` in `id`.** The
permission is fixed; the Switch just isn't there. If the log has no "RCM device connected" line before the ✗,
the app was injecting into nothing: do steps 2-4 above again (2026-11-20: after the restart, `lsusb` showed no Switch at all).

**Nothing at all happens when plugging in.** Check the Switch shows up: `lsusb | grep 0955` should print
`0955:7321 NVIDIA Corp. ... recovery mode`. If not, it isn't in RCM (a Nintendo logo means it booted
normally; RCM also ends after a while, so re-enter it and replug) or the cable carries only power.
